pages.title: Buckyball Cage
pages.text: Sixty carbon atoms bonded into the shape of a football - twelve pentagons and twenty hexagons - with a hollow centre big enough to trap one more atom. It is round, slippery and perfectly symmetrical, and the hollow seems to be waiting for something.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Heating graphene with blaze powder, I expected soot. Instead the sheets curled into closed spheres, and cooled in superfluid helium they stayed that way - the same cages Kroto and Smalley found in vaporised graphite.
